extracted.intended_audience: people who create or might submit online math explanations (students, teachers, math enthusiasts, content creators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting to the Summer of Math Exposition (SoME3): create an online math explanation (video, blog post, or other) loosely related to math, submit by the deadline, and participate in a peer-review pairwise voting system that seeds an in-house selection of winners and honorable mentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic relevance / focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should be 'loosely related to math' and have 'a lesson worth sharing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement explicitly allows essentially any topic as long as it is loosely related to math; the emphasis is on producing a useful explanation or lesson rather than fitting a narrow subject area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted formats
rubrics_metrics.description: You could make a video, a blog post, or whatever else you dream up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format is flexible — videos, blog posts, or other creative formats are acceptable. The page encourages creativity rather than enforcing a strict format requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility / intended submitters
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to students, teachers, or just math enthusiasts — anyone who has a lesson worth sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No narrow professional qualification is required; the event is intended to encourage a broad range of creators to produce math explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are due August 18th; submit via https://some.3b1b.co/register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't submit an entry you may still register to participate in the peer review session. Use the provided registration link to sign up before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation method — pairwise peer review voting
rubrics_metrics.description: After the submission deadline, participants use a system that successively shows them two different entries and asks them to vote on which is best, 'according to a few criteria we lay out.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The core peer-review mechanism is pairwise comparisons; participants compare two entries at a time and choose the better one. The page notes that the actual voting asks raters to judge based on a few criteria (not detailed on this page). Peer review is positioned both as an evaluation mechanism and as a way to help creators discover each other's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation algorithm and in-house review
rubrics_metrics.description: An underlying algorithm uses pairwise rankings to generate an ordered list of all entries; this ordering is used as a starting point for an in-house review of the top entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organizer personally reviews roughly the top 100 entries produced by the algorithm over about two weeks, then convenes others from the math-communication community to select final winners. The page notes the algorithmic ordering 'isn't perfect' but provides a manageable shortlist for deeper manual review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility / exposure as part of the process
rubrics_metrics.description: The concentrated peer-review period and subsequent featuring of winners/honorable mentions produces substantial exposure for entries (previous years' entries collectively accumulated many millions of views).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not an explicit judging criterion, participating in the peer-review period and being selected as a winner or honorable mention confers visibility (e.g., being featured in a 3Blue1Brown summary video). The announcement frames exposure as a benefit and a practical effect of the selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: You can register to participate in peer review even if you don't submit an entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organizers encourage broad participation in the peer-review session to both improve the selection process and to help creators gain early viewership; registering without submitting is explicitly allowed.
